pr.title: Plan showing projects proposed in open pull requests
pr.head: 15cb40d18e911face2cd2393af143b526d6392e9

summary: Projector's site has a Projects page that lists every plan under docs/projects/ on the default branch. Projector writes each new plan as a pull request so people review it before it merges, so while a plan is in review the Projects page, the site's search, and the links from review pages all leave it out. The plan's text is already on the site, though: each published summary stores its pull request's diff as diff.patch, and the diff of a new file holds every line of that file.
This pull request adds one plan, proposed-projects, at status: ready and priority: next. It changes no code. The plan has the site build do the following:

1. Find proposed plans. For each open pull request, the build reads its newest summary and picks each readme.md that the diff adds as a new file under the projects directory.
  2. Rebuild and parse them. It rebuilds the file's text from the diff's added lines and parses it with the same code that project list runs.
  3. Show them as proposed. It lists each one on the Projects page in its status group with a Proposed badge, and opens its page at projects/<name>/ with a banner that names the pull request.

The build reads only the summaries, so it makes no new GitHub request and shows nothing that the Reviews section does not already show. A plan already on the default branch always wins over a proposal, and the lowest pull request number wins a name that two pull requests propose.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Summary: the review page data that project summary publish stores on refs/projector/summaries, with the pull request's diff beside it.
  • Checkout: the branch the site is built from, the default branch on a deploy.
  • Proposed project: a plan that an open pull request's newest summary adds and the checkout lacks.
  • Nested project: a project inside another project's folder, such as alpha/beta.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The first review, at 15cb40d, requested changes with one finding. Step 9 of § 2.1 drops a proposed nested plan whose top-level folder has no project. It claims to mirror the checkout, but the checkout keeps such a plan on the site and only prints a warning. The flag on line 102 carries the finding.

groups.title: The proposed-projects plan
groups.kicker: A ready plan for listing plans that open pull requests add
intro: The plan is the whole change. Read it in order: § 1 says what the site misses today, § 2 gives the design step by step, § 3 gives the reasons and the rejected names and sources, and § 4 lists the tests the implementing pull request must add.
Because the plan is at ready, it claims that someone can implement it without asking further questions. Check each claim it makes about the current code, since an implementer will build on them.

files.note: The new plan. It names the functions it changes in src/projector/site/__init__.py, src/projector/summary.py, src/projector/core.py, src/projector/cli.py, and site/src/site.ts.

checks.text: § 2.1 is the build's algorithm. Today build_summaries links each summary to projects while it reads the summaries, and asks GitHub for each pull request's state afterwards. The plan reorders that: read, ask for states, find proposed plans, then link over both lists.

Step 2 only moves an existing call. I read build_summaries: it calls status_lookup once for each pull request, after linking, and the statuses test in tests/test_site.py asserts one call per pull request. Nothing before linking needs a route, so assign_routes can also run after the proposed projects join the list.

Step 9 drops a proposed nested plan whose top-level folder holds no project, and § 7 says the checkout does the same. It does not: site_projects only warns about missing-plan, and a site built from a checkout with omega/x/readme.md and no omega/readme.md lists omega/x. With this step, such a plan is hidden while proposed and appears once merged. The review asks to remove the step and its § 4 row, and to correct § 7.
Step 10 does not say whether it skips Markdown under a hidden folder, such as gamma/.notes/x.md. The checkout skips those through pages_under. The review lists this as a suggestion, not a blocker.
§ 2.3 keeps the word in one constant, PROPOSED, and adds a badge proposed link to the pull request's review page wherever the site lists the project.

Proposed content is served as Markdown only. showHtml loads an HTML page in an iframe on the site's own origin without a sandbox attribute, so an unmerged page's script could read the rest of the site.

I read parse_diff in src/projector/summary.py: it sets new from new file mode, keeps every added line, and records \ No newline at end of file as a meta line, so new_file_text can rebuild a new file from its output.
This is the claim the flag on line 102 corrects. invalid-project plans are left out, and README.md is not loaded as a project, but nested projects under a missing-plan folder stay on the site.
